subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should a manually selected `openai/*` session keep switching to the Codex harness when the `codex` plugin becomes available, or should OpenClaw preserve the prior OpenClaw runtime unless Codex is explicitly selected?
rationale: Current source, docs, and tests define strict `/model` session pins plus OpenAI-to-Codex default routing, but the report shows that behavior can be confused with the plugin overriding a non-OpenAI primary after hot reload.

options.title: Keep contract, improve diagnostics
options.body: Preserve strict `openai/*` session pins and OpenAI-to-Codex default routing, but make `/status`, Doctor, or support guidance clearly show the pin and `/model default` recovery path.

options.title: Change runtime transition semantics
options.body: Treat plugin enablement as insufficient to move an existing OpenAI session pin onto Codex unless the user explicitly selects Codex, which needs compatibility and upgrade proof.

options.title: Fold into #87957 resolver
options.body: Route the user scenario into the broader session model/auth state resolver so run, display, inherited, and stale state semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Keep contract, improve diagnostics
recommendation.body: Preserve strict `openai/*` session pins and OpenAI-to-Codex default routing, but make `/status`, Doctor, or support guidance clearly show the pin and `/model default` recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current and historical signal across OpenAI runtime policy, selected-session resolution, and Codex harness routing.
